name: Anysite
subcategory: AI web scraping and structured extraction
tagline: AI-assisted web scraper that turns arbitrary pages into structured data you can export or pull via API.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The core trick, point a headless browser at a page, dump the readable DOM, ask a model to fill a JSON schema, is genuinely a one-session build and it works well on cooperative sites. What you are actually paying for is everything after that: residential proxies, captcha and bot-wall handling, retries, a browser farm that does not fall over on a thousand URLs, and someone else eating the maintenance when a target site reshuffles its markup. For a personal project scraping a few dozen pages a week, the DIY version is fine and cheaper. For anything at volume or behind Cloudflare, you will spend your weekend fighting infrastructure instead of parsing data. Also worth remembering that scraped-data pipelines break quietly, and the hosted version at least tells you when it did.
coreLoopDIY: A local CLI that renders a URL in a headless browser, extracts the readable content, and has an LLM fill a JSON schema you define, then writes JSON or CSV.
requirements: Node 20+ and Playwright with a Chromium download
An LLM API key in .env (OpenAI or Anthropic)
Willingness to hand-tune selectors when a target site changes
Your own IP, which some targets will rate limit or block
whatYouLose: Proxy rotation and residential IPs, so bot walls and geo-gated pages stay closed
Captcha handling and stealth fingerprinting that actually survives Cloudflare
Managed concurrency, so large crawls mean building your own queue and retry logic
A hosted API endpoint and scheduling, your version runs when your laptop is awake
Someone else maintaining extraction when target sites redesign
moatNotes: The moat is boring and expensive: IP pools, browser fleets, and the long tail of sites that actively do not want to be read.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because scraping is not a parsing problem, it is an adversarial networking problem. Anyone can extract fields from HTML with a model in an afternoon; almost nobody wants to own a proxy budget, a captcha vendor relationship, and a pager for when a target flips its anti-bot config. Paying converts an ongoing maintenance liability into a line item, which is exactly the trade most people should make once they are scraping at any real volume.
notes: Build it for your own twenty URLs, buy it the moment you have twenty thousand.
prompt:
Build a local CLI tool called "scrape-to-schema" in an empty folder.

Stack, no substitutions: TypeScript, Node 20, Playwright (Chromium), Zod for schema validation, Commander for the CLI, and the OpenAI SDK for extraction. No web UI, no database, no server.

What it does:
1. `scrape-to-schema run --url <url> --schema ./schema.json --out ./out.json`
2. Launch Playwright Chromium (headless by default, `--headful` flag for debugging), navigate, wait for network idle with a timeout, scroll to the bottom once to trigger lazy loading.
3. Strip the DOM down: remove script, style, svg, nav, footer, and aria-hidden nodes, then serialize the remaining visible text plus anchor hrefs into a compact markdown-ish string. Truncate to a configurable token budget.
4. Read the user's JSON Schema file, convert it to a Zod validator, and call the model in JSON mode asking it to fill exactly that schema from the page text. Retry up to 3 times on validation failure, feeding back the validation error.
5. Write validated output as JSON, and also CSV if `--csv` is passed and the schema root is an array.

Also support `--urls ./urls.txt` for batch mode with a concurrency limit (default 3), a polite delay flag, and a `--cache ./.cache` directory that stores raw HTML by URL hash so re-runs do not re-fetch.

Respect robots.txt by default with a `--ignore-robots` opt-out that prints a warning.

Secrets: read OPENAI_API_KEY from .env via dotenv. Ship a .env.example. Never log the key.

Explicitly out of scope, do not build: proxy rotation, captcha solving, stealth plugins, login flows, scheduling, a hosted API, telemetry, or user accounts.

Deliver: package.json with scripts, tsconfig, src/ split into cli.ts, browser.ts, extract.ts, schema.ts, an example schema.json for scraping a product listing page, and a README with one working end-to-end command. Include a single smoke test that runs the extractor against a local HTML fixture with a stubbed model response.
